posts.title: Anna Biller: “A witch is a metaphor for a woman.”
posts.description: A witch is a metaphor for a woman. When you’re a woman you always feel like an outsider or different in some way — abnormal — because the male is seen as the standard human being. That can be good or bad, like you can bewitch a man or curse a man, you can be put on a pedestal or burned at the stake. But I think men essentially see us as witches, and I wanted to go into how that feels, that experience of being treated like a dangerous outsider with every little thing you do. I feel like that especially when I’m directing, like people are looking at me askance because there’s a right way to make a film and I’m doing it wrong, and some more normal, reasonable person needs to step in and save me. posts.title: Quotes from Inheritors of the Earth by Chris D. Thomas
posts.description: “The default stance of conservation is to keep things as unchanged as possible or, alternatively, to return conditions to what they used to be, or somehow to make the Earth ‘more natural’ (which can usually be interpreted as meaning ‘with reduced human impact’). Not only are these untenable aspirations while the world’s human population continues to grow and each of us consumes more resources, but hold-the-line strategies implicitly dismiss as undesirable the continuing biological gains of the human epoch. Where is the logic in this? Attempting to prevent the establishment of ‘alien’ arrivals and to kill ‘impure’ new hybrids so as to maintain our ecosystems and species in some idealized state is not possible, nor is it obvious that the past state of the world is objectively preferable to the new state that is coming into existence.” -page 8 “Rearrangement followed by rearrangement is the norm.
